[Search] Results for 'What is the full title of the work of literature known by its Greek title Oedipus Tyrannus?':
[Doc 1] Oedipus Rex: Oedipus Rex, also known by its Greek title, Oedipus Tyrannus (Ancient Greek: Οἰδίπους Τύραννος IPA: [oidípuːs týranːos]), or Oedipus the King, is an Athenian tragedy by Sophocles that was first performed around 429 BC.

[Doc 2] Oedipus Rex:  Originally, to the ancient Greeks, the title was simply "Oedipus" ("Οἰδίπους"), as it is referred to by Aristotle in the "Poetics".

[Doc 3] Satyricon:  As with the "Metamorphoses" (also called "The Golden Ass") of Apuleius, classical scholars often describe it as a "Roman novel", without necessarily implying continuity with the modern literary form.

[Doc 4] Spirit of the Border:  A highly romanticized account, the novel is the second in a trilogy, the first of which is "Betty Zane", Grey's first published work, and "The Last Trail", which focuses on the life of Jonathan Zane, Grey's ancestor.

[Doc 5] Satyricon: The Satyricon, or Satyricon "liber" ("The Book of Satyrlike Adventures"), is a Latin work of fiction believed to have been written by Gaius Petronius, though the manuscript tradition identifies the author as a certain Titus Petronius.
